sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The ABS failures already on the record cluster around firms that forgot they are law firms. Lynda Shely reports that two compliance lawyers have been disciplined and reads that as proof the system works, but the operator takeaway is that the named ethics officer is the first person exposed when a firm slips [OdPOa3osKC0 @ 00:10:44]. Shely also warns against the cheap compliance-lawyer model: the role needs management experience, and one person should not be stretched across five to seven firms [OdPOa3osKC0 @ 00:19:39]. The sharpest trap hits mass-tort and PI operators, who made up 26 of the 65 ABS firms counted in the three-year update: a bar complaint is pending over a firm allegedly just referring cases out, and Shely states an Arizona lawyer must give substantive input on intake, medical-record review and client communication, so an empty Arizona office funneling cases to Florida is not allowed [poe1CAsUc4U @ 00:36:28]. On the Law Leaders update, Shely closes with the line every tort aggregator should keep in view: this is not a get-rich-quick scheme, even though ER 7.2's elimination now lets Arizona lawyers pay non-lawyers referral fees as a percentage of fees, with no bar charges so far [Tvn12qG9i5s @ 00:27:40].

On the healthcare side, the failures that blow up MSO structures are mundane and operational. Holt Law's warning example is a clinic posting before-and-after photos without patient consent and running QuickBooks payroll that was misfiled with missed taxes, exactly the back-office work an MSO is supposed to absorb [bXO6V29iXPs @ 00:03:37]. The structural leak Holt Law flags is owners pushing clinical assets such as lasers over to the MSO side, when a conservative read keeps Botox, filler, clinical salaries and even medical equipment inside the clinical entity [Oa-6OBD0Gak @ 00:04:04]. Erin Jackson cautions that an MSO is never a single filing: it needs additional contracts and a medical director to keep non-physician operators clear of the practice of medicine, and the private-equity exit story carries no guarantees on what PE may be interested in [4niOtoceEKc @ 00:01:15]. CorporateAttorneysCA lists the downstream penalty stack: regulatory issues can arise around the corporate practice of medicine, fee splitting and the Stark law, which can result in serious consequences if violated [cTWDG8n6ks0 @ 00:01:56]. The economics check is simple: if the MSA, the asset split and the medical director are not airtight, the efficiency pitch becomes the liability.

Deal-side traps hit before and after closing. Frederick Shelton warns that some investment bankers overpromise 10x multiples to collect $1 million to $2 million success fees, while an actual offer of 4x profit compares poorly with the 6x to 8x Shelton sees in the market, and closing before January can hand 30% to 40% to taxes [I4F5OYZQJuU @ 00:24:08]. Shelton's governance kill-switch is a board with one attorney facing four PE directors who control equity-partner decisions, which Shelton labels controlling the practice of law [I4F5OYZQJuU @ 00:31:10]. Holt Law adds two post-close risks: investor pressure on the firm, and the fact that lawyers often cannot be bound by non-competes, so the only shield is an ironclad MSA [DNk78wbKy5s @ 00:05:58]. Kvesic frames the traditional partnership as its own failure mode: partners sweep cash to zero in December, run on a January credit line, and resume draws in March or April, which Kvesic calls a ridiculous way to run a business, while a bank loan simply adds a creditor with liens on receivables [_P68fUIZN48 @ 00:24:17]. Before signing, operators should price the multiple, the closing date, the board seats and the non-compete gap together, not one at a time.

callout.title: Four kill-switch checks before signing an MSO or ABS deal
callout.body: Each check below comes straight from a trap a practitioner reported firsthand. Fail any one and the structure that was supposed to unlock capital becomes the exposure.
items: Confirm an Arizona-admitted lawyer personally handles intake, medical-record review and client communication; an empty Arizona office funneling cases elsewhere is not allowed [The Heart of Law Podcast — poe1CAsUc4U @ 00:36:28].
Reject any MSO compensation pegged to a percentage of the law firm's revenue; stick to flat monthly or cost plus fair margin [Holt Law: For Healthcare Businesses — DNk78wbKy5s @ 00:02:51].
Walk from any buyer whose pitch is that controlling client intake means controlling the firm [Ten Golden Rules Internet Marketing for Law Firms — I4F5OYZQJuU @ 00:28:35].
Hire a compliance lawyer with management experience who is not spread across five to seven firms [The Heart of Law Podcast — OdPOa3osKC0 @ 00:19:39].

chapters.pull_quote: "An ABS law firm is a law firm, it is not a referral service." — The Heart of Law Podcast (poe1CAsUc4U @ 00:35:25).
action_checklist: Determine first whether the business counts as the practice of medicine; if it does, set up an MSO with a physician partner (Dike Law Group | Texas Healthcare Law, aZDpDRV6-KA @ 00:01:06).

Split into two companies: the medical entity employs the doctors, and the MSO runs janitorial, reception, billing and non-medical hiring and firing (Jackson LLP Healthcare Lawyers, wUqthLNx6Ro @ 00:01:00).
Price the MSA as a flat monthly fee or cost plus a fair margin, never as a percentage of revenue (Holt Law: For Healthcare Businesses, DNk78wbKy5s @ 00:03:05).

Before filing an Arizona ABS application, disclose every person or company with a 10% or greater interest, including holding companies and decision-makers, and document plans for confidentiality, trust accounting, conflicts and docketing (The Heart of Law Podcast, poe1CAsUc4U @ 00:18:08).
Build a firewall where the non-lawyer side runs product, operations and capital while only attorneys quote fees and handle engagement letters (LegalTechLIVE, ajveDNkk7dg @ 00:22:41).
After closing, keep the brand and staff in place and give key non-attorneys equity in the MSO (Ten Golden Rules Internet Marketing for Law Firms, I4F5OYZQJuU @ 00:33:48).
